claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element automotive alloy containing nearly equiatomic active elements and low platinum content.
The intervention is a single low-temperature oxidation post-treatment in humidified air containing NO.
The proposed treatment is performed at approximately 250°C for several hours in air containing about 5% water vapor and a low concentration of NO.
Controlled oxidation will form a stable, oxygen-deficient mixed-oxide surface layer on the multi-element catalyst.
The mixed-oxide surface layer will contain a high density of oxygen vacancies.
The oxygen vacancies will act as redox-active sites.
The oxide surface layer will inhibit sintering and preserve the dispersion of catalytically active sites.
Selective oxidation during the treatment will produce a robust oxygen-deficient oxide film.
An increased abundance of oxygen vacancies will enhance metal-oxide redox processes.
The oxygen-deficient oxide layer will increase oxygen-storage capacity.
The surface modification will stabilize active sites against deactivation caused by water and NO.
Prevention of excessive sintering will mitigate degradation caused by thermal aging.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the treated catalyst will have improved catalytic activity at low temperature.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the treated catalyst will retain activity better during transient operation, repeated thermal cycling, and simulated extended mileage.
The untreated catalyst loses activity and durability during low-temperature transient operation involving H2O, NO, and thermal aging.
The expected benefits apply over an exhaust operating range of 150–350°C with transient exposure to water vapor and NO.
Substantially higher treatment temperatures or materially different treatment-gas compositions may not provide the proposed benefits.
